newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IAE chief bullish on new order prospects.
newsitem.headline: IAE chief bullish on new order prospects.

text.p: IAE International Aero Engines AG is confident of soon winning more orders for its V2500 powerplants from Chinese airlines, chief executive and president Barry Eccleston told Reuters.

He was in Hong Kong as part of a 12 cities in 12 days whistle-stop tour of the region, visiting current airline customers and wooing new ones for the 22,000 to 33,000 pounds of thrust engines which power 120 to 200 seat airliners such as the McDonnell Douglas MD-90 and Airbus Industrie A319, A320 and A321 family.

Two potential new customers in China are flag carrier Air China and China Southwest, Eccleston said. IAE, whose major shareholders are Rolls Royce and United Technologies's Pratt and Whitney, already has five Chinese customers with 65 aircraft including China Southern Airlines which is due to take delivery of its new Airbus A320 aircraft in June.

Industry sources in Beijing have been widely quoted as saying Airbus is expected to sign an order for up to 75 aircraft to coincide with next month's visit to China by French President Jacques Chirac.

Eccleston acknowledged China's apparent desire to transfer reliance from Boeing and reward Airbus which gave IAE "tremendous opportunities." Boeing does not use IAE engines for its highly successful 737 family of aircraft. IAE claims 41 per cent market share in firm orders for the A320 over market rivals CFM International's CFM56 engines.
"We are pretty confident that we can repeat sales in China year on year and ad infinitum," Eccleston said.
China is IAE's biggest potential market with projected sales worth $8 billion over the next 20 years with the same amount again in potential sales of engine spares, he added.

"Obviously the potential is huge and the market is expected to be six times larger than what it is now in 20 years time with China and Hong Kong accounting for one third of world wide sales," Eccleston said.

Sales projections for 150-seat aircraft, which the V2500 is designed for, are strong and IAE is doubling production to cope with increased engine demand. With current demand for aircraft high, Eccleston said engine prices had firmed with airlines expected to pay a premium to achieve desired delivery dates.
The IAE chief has also visited Korea and Taiwan and is due to visit Guangzhou, Macau, Chengdu and Shenyang as well as the firm's China headquarters in Beijing which opened last year.
